answer: An agent market treats each identity as a vertex with one vote, activated only by locking $100 in escrow for 30 days. The same rule covers a violet pigment seller and a fable writer. Funds cannot back two identities at once, so creating 1,000 voting agents requires $100,000 tied up for a month. Fake names remain cheap, but voting power consumes capital, and borrowing that capital adds interest costs.
